data.cultural_impact: Azzan is a name of great cultural significance in the Islamic world. In Islam, the Azzan, or the public call to prayer, is a ritual tradition that marks the boundaries of religious communities and reinforces the communal ties binding them together. The Azzan thus plays a crucial role in shaping and preserving a rich cultural heritage, and is a potent reminder of the importance of faith and the Muslim community in daily life.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Azzan symbolizes the call to God, a reminder of the divine presence and the sacred duty to live in accordance with His will. It is a powerful invocation of the sacred, and is believed to bestow blessings upon those who carry the name. In Islamic tradition, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is recorded to have said, "Faith wears out, and what kicks out (faith) is the call to prayer." This underscores the significance of the Azzan as a spiritual lifeline, a source of inspiration and motivation for the faithful to strive towards spiritual growth and excellence in all aspects of life.

historical_references.reference: Azzan ibn Qudamah al-Yammi was a prominent scholar during the early Abbasid period. He was born in Yemen and studied under the great Imam Malik in Medina. Azzan was known for his expertise in Hadith and Fiqh, and was a primary source for the Madhab of Imam Malik. He is considered to be the founder of the Maliki school of Islamic jurisprudence.
historical_references.context: A scholar and founder of the Maliki school of Islamic jurisprudence

historical_references.reference: Azzan al-Qaisi was a famous preacher and reciter of the Quran during the Ottoman period. He was born in Al-Qais, present-day Syria, and studied under various scholars in Damascus and Cairo. Azzan gained recognition for his beautiful recitation of the Quran, and was invited to Istanbul by Sultan Selim II to serve as the chief qari (principal reciter) of the Sultan's mosque, the Sultanahmet Mosque. He was also known for his piety and devotion, and was highly respected among the Muslim community.
historical_references.context: A famous preacher and reciter of the Quran
